title: BI starts with decisions, not data
course_title: Business Intelligence Basics: Designing Systems that Drive Decisions

say: BI starts with decisions, not data.
This is the video for Module 1 of Business Intelligence Basics: what BI is and where it fits.
Many businesses already have plenty of data. The POS terminal records card payments, Paystack or Moniepoint keeps every transfer, and the shop has a stock book.

say: Yet on Monday morning the owner asks, how much did we really sell last week, and what should I reorder? And nobody can answer quickly with confidence.

say: In this course, BI means a repeating system that gets the right information to the right decision-maker at the right time, so a decision is made and acted on.

say: First, source systems, where data is born: the POS, payment apps, accounting software, WhatsApp order lists, even paper registers.

panel.heading: The six links in the BI chain
items: Source systems: where data is born
Decision and action by a named person

say: Next, collect and clean: getting data out and fixing spellings, duplicates and gaps. Professionals call this ETL, which means extract, transform, load.

panel.heading: The six links in the BI chain
items: Source systems: where data is born
Decision and action by a named person

say: Then one trusted store. For a small business, that can be one well-structured Google Sheet.

panel.heading: The six links in the BI chain
items: Source systems: where data is born
Decision and action by a named person

say: Then defined metrics, so that sales means the same thing in every report.

panel.heading: The six links in the BI chain
items: Source systems: where data is born
Decision and action by a named person

say: Then the reports and alerts themselves, such as a weekly one-page summary, or a WhatsApp message when stock is low.

panel.heading: The six links in the BI chain
items: Source systems: where data is born
Decision and action by a named person

say: And last, a named person looks at the information on a known day and decides something. Without this link, the rest is decoration.

items: Source systems: where data is born

panel.rule: If any link breaks, the whole chain fails.

say: BI designers do not start with what data do we have. They ask, what decisions does this business make again and again? The tool is a decision inventory.
For example, Funmi runs a frozen chicken and fish business in Ibadan with two cold rooms.

say: OLTP systems run the business. They record each sale, payment or enrolment, and must be fast.

panel.heading: Running the business vs answering questions
left: Records one sale at a time
Must be fast and always on

say: OLAP means storage built for analysis: adding thousands of rows and comparing months. BI copies data into a separate store, so reports do not slow down the till and history is kept.

say: Before you recommend anything, find the starting point. At level 1, data is scattered in notebooks, phones and people's heads.
At level 2, monthly reports are built by hand from exports, and numbers often disagree.
At level 3, one trusted store exists, and standard reports refresh on schedule.
At level 4, metrics have owners, quality checks and access rules.
At level 5, reports are used in fixed review meetings, and actions are tracked.
A 10-question check helps. Score each question 0 for no, 1 for partly, or 2 for yes. The maximum is 20.

panel.heading: Scoring a cooperative
items: Next step: definitions and one register

say: For example, Hauwa runs a cooperative in Kaduna with about 600 members. Contributions are recorded in two Excel files that often disagree. Her total is 6.

panel.heading: Scoring a cooperative
items: Next step: definitions and one register

say: A score of 6 to 9 means level 2, spreadsheet reporting.

panel.heading: Scoring a cooperative
items: Next step: definitions and one register

say: So her next step is written definitions and one trusted register, not a dashboard. Buying a dashboard tool too early shows wrong numbers, and leaders stop trusting data altogether.

panel.heading: Scoring a cooperative
items: Next step: definitions and one register
panel.rule: Fix the foundations before you buy a dashboard tool.

say: To remember. BI is a repeating system, not a tool, and every link must work, right up to the action.
Start with a decision inventory, keep reporting separate from the till, and know the maturity level before you build.
